title: Typed fragment callbacks and degraded emission guidelines (PRD addendum)
creator: Miguel Ortega
description: Addendum to the existing PRD that defines semantics, observability, and acceptance tests for typed fragment emission when model output is delivered incrementally and when function/tool callbacks are invoked in degraded conditions. This document clarifies scope changes requested by reliability and SDK teams: we now require explicit fragment commit markers, a lightweight fragment reconciliation protocol, and deterministic idempotency semantics for function callbacks across retries and partial replays. The addendum covers schema expectations for partial frames, error categories and recovery steps, backpressure negotiation, and telemetry keys required for post-mortem and SLA verification.
acceptance_tests: Fragment framing: client receives a sequence of typed frames where each frame includes 'fragment_id', 'seq_no', 'total_estimate' (optional) and 'commit' boolean; frames are applied in order and a final commit frame marks the completed object

Partial object reconstruction: given a stream with dropped middle frames (simulated network loss), SDK must reconstruct best-effort object and flag 'partial:true' until a commit arrives; server must emit reconciliation hint when missing seq_no detected

Idempotent function-calls: function/tool invocations made by the model must include a deterministic invocation_id; retries (client or server-initiated) with the same invocation_id must be treated as duplicates by tool gateway and should not cause side-effect duplication

Failure modes classification: tests to verify clear categorization into transient (retryable), permanent (client-visible error), and partial-commit (object partially persisted) with suggested remediation messages

Backpressure & pacing: when downstream tool latency spikes, server reduces fragment emission rate, emits 'throttled' frames and must preserve ordering; SDK test ensures consumer can apply pacing hints without losing semantics

Streaming schema tolerance: when schema version mismatch occurs mid-stream, server must emit 'schema_hint' and 'fallback_frame' with best-effort mapping; SDK must log and surface a schema-mismatch event to the application

Observability hooks: each fragment and function invocation must emit trace_id, fragment_id, invocation_id and a vector of token-latency and kernel-profile tags to the Console; acceptance verifies these fields exist for 100% of test streams

Graceful degradation: when model is evicted mid-response, server emits an explicit 'degraded_end' frame with reason code; clients must map reason codes to human-readable messages and fall back to cached or lower-fidelity model variant
observability_requirements: Traceable invocation_id propagated from model -> router -> tool gateway
Fragment gap detector alerts when out-of-order or missing seq_no is observed
Tool-side deduplication events and side-effect suppression logs
